full_caption: Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust, Appellant, v. Georgiana Alderidge, Appellee
court: Northridge District Court of Appeal, First District
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This action turns on the construction of three riders appended to a commercial lease between Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust, as landlord, and Georgiana Alderidge, as tenant, for 800 square feet at 3364 Kingfisher Drive, Stillwater, NR.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A landlord may not withhold consent in order to extract a rent increase not bargained for in the lease. The demand for 25 percent of the sublease profits, absent a recapture provision, was unreasonable as a matter of law.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The Continuous Operation Rider requires the tenant to remain open during the hours the shopping center is open. It is enforceable by injunction only where damages are inadequate; a going-dark clause with a stated liquidated remedy displaces injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A rider is read as part of the integrated lease. Where a rider and the printed form conflict, the rider controls, because it represents the parties' specific and later-negotiated intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The Late Fee Rider assesses a charge of 3 percent of any installment not received by the 3th day of the month, together with interest at 12 percent per annum on the unpaid balance from the due date.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A late charge and default interest may be imposed cumulatively only where the lease says so expressly. Absent express language, imposing both amounts to a double recovery for the same delay.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The Percentage Rent Rider obligates Georgiana Alderidge to pay 4 percent of annual gross sales in excess of a breakpoint of $875,000, with 'gross sales' defined to exclude returns, sales taxes collected, and inter-store transfers.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The Holdover Rider fixes holdover rent at 1.25 times the last monthly installment. Such a provision is enforceable as liquidated damages where holdover harm is difficult to estimate and the multiplier is not grossly disproportionate.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Internet orders fulfilled from the leased premises fall within the definition of gross sales; orders merely placed at a kiosk on the premises and shipped from a remote warehouse do not.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The Assignment and Subletting Rider conditions transfer on the landlord's consent, 'which shall not be unreasonably withheld.' Reasonableness is measured by objective commercial criteria: the proposed transferee's financial capacity, use, and experience.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Judgment for Georgiana Alderidge on the late-fee and default-interest claim is affirmed; judgment for Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust on the percentage-rent claim is affirmed as modified.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — LATE FEES AND DEFAULT INTEREST
sections.text: If any installment of Base Rent or Additional Rent is not received by Landlord by the 3th day of the month, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to 3 percent of the overdue installment. Amounts remaining unpaid more than thirty (30) days after the due date shall thereafter bear interest at 12 percent per annum. The late charge and default interest are alternative and not cumulative remedies for the same delinquent installment; in no event shall Tenant be charged both for the same period of delay.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — PERCENTAGE RENT
sections.text: In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay 4 percent of Gross Sales in each Lease Year in excess of a breakpoint of $875,000. 'Gross Sales' means all receipts from business conducted at, from, or fulfilled out of the Premises, whether for cash or credit, and expressly includes internet and telephone orders fulfilled from inventory located at the Premises, and expressly excludes: returns and allowances actually credited; sales, excise and similar taxes collected and remitted; transfers of merchandise to other stores of Tenant not made to avoid percentage rent; and receipts from vending machines maintained for employees. Tenant shall deliver a statement of Gross Sales within 30 days after each Lease Year, and Landlord may audit not more than once per Lease Year.

sections.heading: RIDER 6 — ESTOPPEL CERTIFICATES AND SUBORDINATION
sections.text: Within 60 days after written request, Tenant shall execute and deliver a certificate stating the commencement and expiration dates, the amount of Base Rent, the amounts of any prepaid rent and security deposit, and whether to Tenant's knowledge Landlord is in default. Failure to deliver within that period shall be deemed an admission of the accuracy of the statements contained in the form furnished by Landlord. This Lease is subordinate to any mortgage now or hereafter placed on the Center, provided the mortgagee delivers a commercially reasonable non-disturbance agreement.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
